items.sequencingTheme: Accelerate agent-governance rollout after the control plane is already absorbing real decision work.
items.boardQuestion: Which AI lane is ready to move first because the governance spine is already proven?
items.currentPosture: The AI flagship already carries scorecards, memos, and governance packets, so the sequencing question is no longer whether to proceed, but how quickly to widen adoption.
items.requiredProof: Board memo reuse, lower operator drag, and a stable answer layer across agent and protocol workflows.
items.headline: AI governance is the cleanest lane to accelerate first.
items.narrative: The sequencing case is strongest where the control plane is already doing live work instead of waiting on another architecture promise.
items.nextMove: Package agent-governance reuse and memo velocity into the first board-approved acceleration packet.

items.sequencingTheme: Stage identity expansion behind remediation cleanup and stronger operator readiness.
items.boardQuestion: Which security lane matters strategically but still needs sequencing discipline before scale?
items.currentPosture: Identity proof is credible, but exception handling and admin coverage still need a cleaner phased plan before the board approves wider rollout.
items.requiredProof: Lower exception churn, stronger control-owner continuity, and cleaner evidence capture across admin motions.
items.headline: Identity should stage forward in phases, not accelerate all at once.
items.narrative: The right sequencing answer is a controlled phase plan that tightens coverage first and expands scope second.
items.nextMove: Stage identity consolidation behind a narrower remediation proof packet before approving the next expansion phase.

items.sequencingTheme: Defer the next reporting rebuild until attribution integrity and explanation loops improve.
items.boardQuestion: Which revenue-system lane should wait because internal friction still consumes the upside?
items.currentPosture: Reporting and martech surfaces are stronger, but too much operator time still goes into explanation loops and reconciliation rework.
items.requiredProof: Cleaner reporting ownership, lower reconciliation drag, and stronger attribution integrity across releases.
items.headline: Revenue-system expansion should wait until explanation friction drops.
items.narrative: The board should see a defer recommendation here because the upside is still being eaten by operating drag.
items.nextMove: Defer the next reporting rebuild and prove lower reconciliation effort before reopening the investment ask.

items.sequencingTheme: Escalate fragmented proof and sequencing risk before promising another finance-systems push.
items.boardQuestion: Which lane still has too many disconnected motions to sequence safely without executive intervention?
items.currentPosture: Payments, treasury, merchant review, and KYC all exist, but the sequencing story is still fragmented across too many isolated proofs.
items.requiredProof: Shared ownership, coordinated queue design, and one clearer investment path across the FinTech family.
items.headline: FinTech needs escalation before another growth-sequencing claim reaches leadership.
items.narrative: The correct board move is to force one coherent sequencing packet instead of pretending fragmented proofs add up to readiness.
items.nextMove: Escalate fragmented queues and thin operating continuity into one diligence-first sequencing brief.

items.sequencingTheme: Accelerate the buyer-answer core now that procurement packaging is already reusable.
items.boardQuestion: Which buyer-facing lane is ready to move sooner because the answer system already scales?
items.currentPosture: Procurement and trust evidence are already consolidated enough that the next move is scaling distribution, not proving the concept again.
items.requiredProof: Shorter cycle times, fewer custom packets, and wider answer reuse across buyer workflows.
items.headline: Procurement is ready to accelerate through the reusable answer core.
items.narrative: This is the cleanest sequencing case outside AI because the infrastructure for buyer trust already exists.
items.nextMove: Accelerate the answer-core rollout and package cycle-time wins into one board-readable buyer-path memo.

items.sequencingTheme: Stage biotech expansion behind stronger regulated-team continuity and evidence reuse.
items.boardQuestion: Which regulated lane should grow in controlled phases rather than all at once?
items.currentPosture: The biotech family is credible, but the board still needs steadier evidence that review teams can absorb more load without reopening control gaps.
items.requiredProof: Stable case flow, lower review churn, and one continuity packet across GxP, CAPA, specimen, and safety lanes.
items.headline: Biotech should expand in staged phases with continuity proof leading the sequence.
items.narrative: The board story is growth with guardrails, not another broad claim that regulated teams can absorb unlimited volume.
items.nextMove: Stage biotech growth behind a continuity packet that proves review teams can expand safely.
